title: Factors Leading To Reform Movements
definition: The 19th-century Socio-Religious Reform Movements (SRRM) were a response to the stagnation of Indian society, triggered by the collision between traditional Indian values and modern Western rationalism introduced by British colonial rule.
importanceInUpsc: This topic forms the bedrock of Modern Indian History. UPSC frequently tests the causal link between colonial policies, intellectual awakening, and the rise of Indian Nationalism.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Factors Leading To Reform Movements.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Impact of British Rule on Indian Economy
